citation: John Lewis Krimmel, Sunday Morning in front of the Arch Street Meeting House, Philadelphia, 1811-ca. 1813. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 42.95.17.
author: John Lewis Krimmel
repository: The Metropolitan Museum of Art; object 12749 in the museum's collection API (isPublicDomain: true), image DP276569 at images.metmuseum.org.
locator: Open-access image DP276569: the five figures on the pavement.
rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Proposed for use only as a reference picture the 1812 figures are judged against; nothing traced or sampled.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (dress research for the 1812 scene). Watercolour. Two young women in white and cream high-waisted gowns with long sleeves, close bonnets and blue gloves, one with a parasol; an older woman in a brown gown and black bonnet; an older man in a drab coat, breeches and broad hat; a boy of about eight in a dark short jacket and long trousers with a white collar and a round hat.
note: Proposed for the 1812 dress reference sets; not a Chicago or Fort Dearborn record. Added for the 1812 women's dress (T-3464 dress build, tools/human_women_1812.py) from docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json.

a boy's jacket-and-trousers suit and round hat 1811-1813
what_it_does_not_supply: a frontier household; the sitters are Philadelphia Quakers
